text:
sam: quick question after the offload RFC: are we leaning toward slab-shadow ownership swaps or a tag-based mover that physically compacts? pros/cons?
anya: slab-shadow = metadata-only ownership transfer. cheap, fast fairness fixes. con: fragmentation still accumulates; compaction deferred.
leo: tag-based mover actually consolidates but costs memcpy/CPU/GPU time. needs safe remap for in-flight kernels.
frank: practical hybrid: do shadow swaps for immediate rebalancing, schedule physical compaction as low-priority background work. avoid cross-node copy unless pressure high.
sam: pinned device buffers are the blocker. shadow-swap ok, but migration fails if pinned_count>0. we should prefer moving host-backed pages first.
anya: agree. add slab flags: ALLOW_SHADOW, IMMUTABLE_IF_PINNED. compactor honors those.
leo: metrics we need: tenant.compactness, slab.shadow_transfers, migration_cpu_seconds, migration_failures.pinned_device. wire them to tenant dashboard.
frank: action items: 1) prototype shadow swap in allocator shim (leo), 2) add slab flags + drain API (anya), 3) dashboard metrics + canary (sam). mem-bot: scheduled canary: shadow-only-test (dev) ETA 3m.
